data.name: Frey
data.gender_notes: Frey is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old Norse ‘fröyr’, meaning ‘lord’, ‘master’. In Norse mythology, Frey was the god of fertility, prosperity, and peace. The name Frey carries the meaning “Lord, Master” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Frey usually hope their child will grow to embody lord, master and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine protection and abundance.
data.etymology: Frey belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord, Master.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Frey total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.
data.cultural_impact: The name "Frey" has its origins in Norse mythology, where Frey was a prominent god. The word 'Frey' is a derivation from the Old Norse word 'fröyr', meaning 'lord', 'master'. This name likely would've held significant cultural meaning for the Norse people, representing power, dominion, and control.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Frey", derived from Old Norse mythology, is rooted in the deity Frey himself. As the god of fertility, prosperity, and peace, Frey represents growth, abundance, and harmony. It is a reminder of the cyclical nature of life, growth, and renewal. Additionally, as a god of peace, Frey is a symbol of harmony, tranquility, and unity, urging individuals to seek inner peace and cohesion with the natural world.
